cases.sentence: Пьеру за ___ пришлось сидеть против Наташи и странная перемена, происшедшая в ней со дня бала, поразила его.
cases.explain: «бостонным столом» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Pierre, as one of the principal guests, had to sit down to boston with Count Rostóv, the general, and the colonel. At the card table he happened to be directly facing Natásha, and was struck by a curious change that had come over her since the ball. She was silent, and not only less pretty than at the ball, but only redeemed from plainness by her look of gentle indifference to everything around.

cases.sentence: Она сидела подле сестры у ___ и неохотно, не глядя на него, отвечала что-то подсевшему к ней Борису.
cases.explain: «чайного стола» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “What’s the matter with her?” thought Pierre, glancing at her. She was sitting by her sister at the tea table, and reluctantly, without looking at him, made some reply to Borís who sat down beside her. After playing out a whole suit and to his partner’s delight taking five tricks, Pierre, hearing greetings and the steps of someone who had entered the room while he was picking up his tricks, glanced again at Natásha.

cases.sentence: Князь Андрей с ___ стоял перед нею и говорил ей что-то.
cases.explain: «бережливо-нежным выражением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy was standing before her, saying something to her with a look of tender solicitude. She, having raised her head, was looking up at him, flushed and evidently trying to master her rapid breathing. And the bright glow of some inner fire that had been suppressed was again alight in her. She was completely transformed and from a plain girl had again become what she had been at the ball.

cases.sentence: И ___ какого-то внутреннего, прежде потушенного огня, опять горел в ней.
cases.explain: «яркий свет» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: «Что-то очень важное происходит между ними», думал Пьер, и радостное и вместе ___ заставляло его волноваться и забывать об игре.
cases.explain: «горькое чувство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Something very important is happening between them,” thought Pierre, and a feeling that was both joyful and painful agitated him and made him neglect the game.

cases.sentence: Когда Пьер подошел к ним, он заметил, что Вера находилась в ___ разговора, князь Андрей (что́ с ним редко бывало) казался смущен.
cases.explain: «самодовольном увлечении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: When Pierre went up to them he noticed that Véra was being carried away by her self-satisfied talk, but that Prince Andréy seemed embarrassed, a thing that rarely happened with him.

cases.sentence: Что́ вы думаете о Натали, может ли она быть постоянна в своих привязанностях, может ли она так, как ___ (Вера разумела себя), один раз полюбить человека и навсегда остаться ему верною?
cases.explain: «другие женщины» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What do you think?” Véra was saying with an arch smile. “You are so discerning, Prince, and understand people’s characters so well at a glance. What do you think of Natáli? Could she be constant in her attachments? Could she, like other women” (Véra meant herself), “love a man once for all and remain true to him forever? That is what I consider true love. What do you think, Prince?”

cases.sentence: — Я думаю, никто так не был courtisée,[512] предметом ухаживанья, как она, — говорила Вера; — но никогда, до самого ___ никто серьезно ей не нравился.
cases.explain: «последнего времени» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I think no one has been more courted than she,” she went on, “but till quite lately she never cared seriously for anyone. Now you know, Count,” she said to Pierre, “even our dear cousin Borís, who, between ourselves, was very far gone in the land of tenderness …” (alluding to a map of love much in vogue at that time).

cases.explain: «опасное дело» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, you know between cousins intimacy often leads to love. Le cousinage est un dangereux voisinage.68 Don’t you think so?”

cases.sentence: — Ты знаешь наши ___ (он говорил о тех масонских перчатках, которые давались вновь избранному брату для вручения любимой женщине).
cases.explain: «женские перчатки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I must … I must have a talk with you,” said Prince Andréy. “You know that pair of women’s gloves?” (He referred to the Masonic gloves given to a newly initiated Brother to present to the woman he loved.) “I … but no, I will talk to you later on,” and with a strange light in his eyes and restlessness in his movements, Prince Andréy approached Natásha and sat down beside her. Pierre saw how Prince Andréy asked her something and how she flushed as she replied.

cases.sentence: Но в это время Берг подошел к Пьеру, настоятельно упрашивая его принять участие в споре между генералом и полковником об ___.
cases.explain: «испанских делах» — after the preposition «об», for location or topic.
cases.translation: But at that moment Berg came to Pierre and began insisting that he should take part in an argument between the general and the colonel on the affairs in Spain.

cases.sentence: Вечер был очень хорош и совершенно такой, как и ___, которые он видел.
cases.explain: «другие вечера» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Berg was satisfied and happy. The smile of pleasure never left his face. The party was very successful and quite like other parties he had seen. Everything was similar: the ladies’ subtle talk, the cards, the general raising his voice at the card table, and the samovar and the tea cakes; only one thing was lacking that he had always seen at the evening parties he wished to imitate. They had not yet had a loud conversation among the men and a dispute about something important and clever. Now the general had begun such a discussion and so Berg drew Pierre to it.

cases.sentence: И дамские, ___, и карты, и за картами генерал, возвышающий голос, и самовар, и печенье; но одного еще недоставало, того, что́ он всегда видел на вечерах, которым он желал подражать.
